summary: Source-anchored research for GKE NodeLocal DNSCache Atlas. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: For Atlas failures, test SRV resolution with dig SRV _mongodb._tcp.<cluster-host>, resolve each returned node hostname, then test TCP connectivity from the affected workload. Non-SRV URIs bypass SRV discovery but still contain hostnames requiring DNS. (low confidence)
GKE enables NodeLocal DNSCache by default in Autopilot, where it cannot be disabled; Standard enables it by default starting at 1.34.1-gke.3720000. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

Signicat’s December 2023 GKE report described CoreDNS NodeLocal forwarding to kube-dns over TCP, a hard-coded dnsmasq worker limit, and latency spikes coinciding with open connections above that limit. The author recommended Cloud DNS for that stack. This is a historical operational report, not an Atlas benchmark. (low confidence)

Signicat’s December 2023 report described a hard-coded 20-child dnsmasq limit in its GKE NodeLocal-to-kube-dns stack. Google’s GKE documentation distinguishes legacy kube-dns through version 1.35 from CoreDNS-based kube-dns in version 1.36 and later, so Signicat’s historical observation is not a universal current GKE limit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)
NodeLocal DNSCache places a DNS cache on each GKE node, reducing central DNS load and lookup latency. It is a Kubernetes DNS optimization, not an Atlas feature. (high confidence)

A July 25, 2025 community report describes intermittent UnknownHostException and server-selection timeouts from GKE Autopilot to peered Atlas despite successful connections. The report supplies no confirmed NodeLocal DNSCache diagnosis or remedy. (low confidence)

NodeLocal forwards external queries through the local metadata server, bypassing kube-dns. For its cache, positive records expire at the lesser of their TTL and 30 seconds; NXDOMAIN expires after five seconds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

DNS egress policies can break NodeLocal resolution. Inspect the actual resolver path and permit its TCP/UDP DNS traffic; a namespace-only selector failed in Argo CD’s historical GKE incident. (medium confidence)

Mercari’s June 2025 engineering account reports a tenfold reduction in kube-dns calls and tenfold to hundredfold fewer DNS errors after NodeLocal rollout. These are workload-specific observations, not measured Atlas improvements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-06-04)

For kube-dns upstream timeout logs, Google suggests increasing kube-dns replicas; that workaround does not apply to metadata-server timeouts. Autopilot does not support the documented kube-dns-autoscaler customization. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)
